ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is runoff volume, and the horizontal axis is months. The runoff volume curve labeled “downstream” reaches a relatively high value around February in the Northern Hemisphere, approximately close to 8000; around July—August it drops to a relatively low level, and then rises slightly. It is not the curve with the highest runoff volume in summer, July—August. The curve labeled “upstream” is relatively high around summer. Then reason: If a river in the Northern Hemisphere is mainly supplied by alpine ice and snow meltwater, usually because summer temperatures are high and meltwater is abundant, runoff volume is greatest in summer; the seasonal variation of groundwater supply is generally relatively small; runoff changes from rainwater supply mainly vary with the rainy season and may show obvious seasonal peaks and troughs. In the figure, the downstream curve has obvious seasonal variation and does not conform to the peak characteristic of summer meltwater supply; it more conforms to the rainwater supply characteristic controlled by seasonal variation in precipitation. Therefore, the most important source of water supply at the downstream hydrological station is rainwater.
